Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? Do you have a background in electrical power engineering, operations research, or a related field, and are you interested in energy systems and markets? As a PhD candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, both in and outside academia. 

The Department of Electric Energy (IEL) at NTNU is seeking a highly motivated candidate for a full-time (100%) PhD position for 3 years as part of the NTNU Energy initiative on Resilient and Integrated Energy Systems. You will join the research group Electricity Markets and Energy System Planning (EMESP) at IEL, where we foster an open, inclusive, and collaborative working environment.

Our work environment is defined by its friendly and supportive atmosphere, with regular gatherings such as professional meetings within the research group, weekly colloquia, shared lunches, and “Friday coffee” sessions to end the week. These formal and informal events offer opportunities to share ideas, celebrate milestones, and build relationships. PhD candidates also organize social activities open to everyone interested, fostering a welcoming and inclusive community.

Your immediate Line Manager will be the Head of Department.
About the project
Globally, electricity demand is increasing and expected to increase in the coming years, supported by higher consumption from industrial actors, increasing electrification and integration of electric vehicles, data centers and other electrical sources. The electrical grid is getting increasingly strained due to the increased load, which needs to handle the power-intense appliances, while also needing to enable more renewable energy production into the power system. In both the EU and Norway, the ageing distribution grid is expected to have challenges in the future year due to the energy transition, needing investments and reinforcements to prevent critical situations such as voltage issues and bottlenecks in the grid. To combat these issues due to long lead time on investments and immature replacement situations, flexibility is seen as a vital part to enable more active operation of the electrical grid to prolong secure operational conditions. Ensuring local flexible resources in local distributional grids can be enabled for grid support and be integrated as part of the operational solutions without impacting their own operational situations to a large degree will be key to understanding and assessing the potential available. 

The objective of this PhD project is to develop new knowledge, models, methods, and analytical insights into how flexible resources can be utilized to provide grid support to the local distribution grid, while also participating in defined electrical markets and balancing markets. The flexible resources aim to maximize their revenues through different market options, and the consequences this will have on the local distribution grid. How upholding local conditions can be performed will be important to enable value-stacking grid services in an efficient manner. Local distributional systems operators (DSOs) might not have defined specific local markets for grid support, and how this service impacts other revenue streams and how TSO-DSO-coordination impacts operations will need to be analyzed. The project will focus on how these local conditions can be accounted for in long-term operational planning by the flexible provider, while also being accounted for during short-term operational decisions and reserve market activation sequences. Use of both active and reactive power to enable efficient grid operations will be a key aspect to approach this work.

The PhD candidate will develop and apply optimization-based models that capture the dynamics of the electricity grid and different flexible providers in the distributional grid (for instance, but not limited to batteries, EV parking lots, industrial demand, etc.). Key focus will be put into methods that can simplify grid information, to reduce the need for grid-sensitive information during operational planning and operation. Regulatory aspects and TSO-DSO coordination schemes will also need to be addressed and investigated as part of the project. 

The PhD candidate will be hosted by the Electricity Markets and Energy Systems Planning (EMESP) group in the Department of Electric Energy at NTNU. The main supervisor will be Associate Professor Kasper Emil Thorvaldsen, with co-supervision from relevant experts in power system operation and optimization, depending on the final methodological focus of the PhD project.

• Carry out research of high quality within the framework described above

• Complete academic training consisting of coursework corresponding to a minimum 30 ECTS
• Contribute to publications in relevant journals and to popular science dissemination
• 
Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions

About the position
We invite applications for a Researcher position in computational chemistry, available at the Hylleraas centre, Department of Chemistry.

The position is for a period of 2 years.

Starting date no later than 01.03.2027.

Place of work is Hylleraas centre, Department of Chemistry at Blindern, Oslo.
Project description
The position is funded by the Research Council of Norway through the Researcher Project for Early Career Scientists (FRIPRO) “APExModel: Addressing Antimicrobial Peptides by Integrating Experiments into Modelling” and lead by Henrique Musseli Cezar. 

Antimicrobial resistance is a critical global health crisis, and new drugs are urgently needed. 

APExModel will establish a set of experimentally-grounded design principles that can aid the development of safer and more effective AMPs. This will be done by developing and applying a new computational framework that integrates experimental data into simulations. The project will also provide: 1) better understanding the molecular mechanisms that govern how AMPs self-assemble in solution, a key factor for their stability and activity; 2) a novel simulation methodology that can accurately model AMPs interacting with cell membranes by using experimental small-angle scattering data to guide the simulations; and 3) insights on the action mechanisms of different AMPs and how they disrupt bacterial membranes.

The most critical R&D challenge is the development of this new simulation methodology. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide access to dynamics at atomic resolution, but limitations in simulation timescale and accuracy may compromise the agreement with experiments. Current integrative approaches are limited to systems with spherical symmetry and cannot adequately model the flat, patch-like membrane used in most MD simulations of AMP-membrane studies. This project will overcome this limitation, adding a capability that is currently missing in the field.

Combining expertise from chemistry, pharmacy, and physics, this interdisciplinary project will produce a new open-source simulation tool and the fundamental knowledge required to establish design principles for AMPs.

jobs.description:
About the position
We invite applications for a full-time position as Associate Professor in cell biology at the Section for Physiology and Cell Biology, Department of Biosciences, Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences, University of Oslo.

The Department of Biosciences seeks an active researcher with a strong publication record within cell biology. The successful applicant should be on an upward trajectory and have strong potential to develop and execute research projects at a high international level. The research should address fundamental questions in cell biology using animal- or plant-based systems and create synergies with current research in the section and department. 

Research in the Section for Physiology and Cell Biology includes physiological adaptations to extreme conditions, comparative immunology, muscle physiology, neural mechanisms of learning and memory in health and disease, plant signalling and development, cellular and molecular mechanisms of disease including stress signalling, hormone action and cancer biology, as well as intracellular membrane trafficking, organelle dynamics, and mechanisms regulating cell migration and organization. The research groups develop and apply advanced technologies including live imaging, molecular tools and gene engineering, omics technologies and bioinformatics.

The Department of Biosciences is organized into four research sections; Section for Physiology and Cell biology (FYSCELL), Section for Environmental and marine biology (EMB), Section for, Ecology, Biodiversity, and Evolution (EBE), and Section for Molecular Biology, Biochemistry and Bioinformatics (MBB). The research at the department focuses on fundamental biological processes from the molecular and cellular level to the population and ecosystem level. The department has recently moved into the new Life Science Building, which brings together researchers and students from chemistry, pharmacy, biosciences and laboratory medicine and provides state-of-the-art research infrastructure. The department provides access to advanced research infrastructure, including state-of-the-art core facilities, field stations, and specialized platforms that support interdisciplinary life science research across multiple disciplines.
Your main tasks will be
• Develop and lead an internationally competitive research programme in cell biology, using animal- or plant-based systems and taking advantage of existing infrastructure and common research facilities.
• Secure external research funding and establish or contribute to national and international research collaborations and initiatives.
• Carry out research-based teaching in cell biology and molecular biology at bachelor´s, master´s and PhD levels, including laboratory-based courses and supervise master’s and PhD students.
• Contribute to the academic development of the section and department through collegial activities, scientific leadership, and administrative duties.What skills are important in this role?
Required qualifications:

• Completed PhD or equivalent doctoral degree in cell biology or a related field, with a strong scientific track record within cell biology
• Documented experience in securing external research funding.
• Applicants must document academic qualifications in cell biology equivalent to an Associate Professor position. Scientific qualifications will be given significant weight, with particular emphasis on the quality and extent of scientific output within cell biology over the last five years, as well as experience with modern experimental research methods and techniques.
• The successful applicant must be able to carry out research-based teaching in cell and molecular biology at bachelor, master and PhD levels including laboratory-based courses and supervise Master and PhD students.
• Pedagogical qualifications and teaching and supervision experience at all levels will be an important factor in the evaluation process and should be well documented in a teaching portfolio. The applicant should describe their qualifications in view of the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) framework which includes:
• Focus on student learning
• A clear development over time
• A researching approach
• A collegial attitude and practice
• Applicants who at the time of appointment cannot document sufficient teaching qualifications (minimum formal requirement is a 200 hours pedagogical programme) will be required to obtain such qualifications within a two-year period.
• The successful candidate must demonstrate mastery of both English and one of the Scandinavian languages as working languages, in order to be able to teach and otherwise be able to participate in all functions the position may involve. Candidates who do not have sufficient mastery of a Scandinavian language (B2 level) at the time of appointment, will be required attain B2 level proficiency in Norwegian within three years of employment.
Desired qualifications:

• Candidates should be able to establish, lead and conduct research projects, also as a collaborator. Experience in scientific and administrative management is an advantage.
• International research networks, outreach activities, collegiality, and the ability to foster a positive working environment will be considered in the evaluation.
• The person appointed will be requested to take on some administrative duties. Hence such experience will be an advantage.
• Experience in utilizing advanced research infrastructure such as those available at the Department of Biosciences and the University of Oslo, and the ability to contribute to their further development, is an advantage.What are we looking for in you?
Personal skills:

• Ability to create and contribute to a well-functioning, inclusive and productive research environment
• Networking skills, ability to collaborate and conduct scientific leadership
• Ability to cooperate and communicate well with other members of staff
The successful candidate should have an international profile consistent with to the above criteria. The candidate will be selected based on documented qualifications and the fit and expertise to strengthen and create synergies with the research profiles of the section and department.
We can offer you
• Exciting and meaningful tasks in an organization with an important societal mission, contributing to knowledge development, education, and enlightenment that promote sustainable, fair, and knowledge-based societal development.
• Committed colleagues in a good working environment. 
• Good welfare schemes.
• Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours.  A workplace with good development and career opportunities.
• Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes.
• Salary in position as Associate Professor (position code 1011) in salary range NOK from 750 000 - to 850 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, two % is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund. We need different perspectives in our work
UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at  UiO's policy for diversity, equality and inclusion.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues; could you be the next one?

We will do our best to meet your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.

If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps (in Norwegian), we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (in Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports.

More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here.
How to apply
The application must include:

• Research plan (up to 5 pages) describing the applicant’s scientific vision and ambitions and how the proposed research will strengthen or create synergies with ongoing research activities in the Section for Physiology and Cell Biology and the Department of Biosciences.
• Detailed CV, including education, positions, pedagogical experience, administrative and management experience, project acquisition and coordination experience, and other qualifying activities.

Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.
General information
As a general rule an interview will be used in the appointment process, usually supplemented with a trial teaching session. The basis for assessment will be the scientific production of the applicant, the teaching portfolio, pedagogical and educational qualifications, the applicant’s qualifications within leadership and administration, other qualifications as well as general personal suitability for the position. In ranking the competent applicants, the full range of qualifications will be considered and explicitly assessed.

According to the Norwegian Freedom and Information Act (Offentleglova), information about the applicant may be included in the public applicant list, also in cases where the applicant has requested non-disclosure.

jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You can find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.

   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WWHqR5i1FHE&feature=youtu.beAbout the Job
The Department of Information Security and Communication Technology (IIK) at NTNU Gjøvik has a vacancy for a Researcher in Socio-Technical Fraud Systems. 

The position is for an intended period of 24 months and is part of SAFE – Secure Anti-Fraud Excellence Center, funded by Sparebankstiftelsen Hedmark and SpareBank 1 Østlandet in collaboration with NTNU and industry partners.The researcher will be a key member of WP1 and lead its socio-technical root cause analysis of financial fraud, hosted at CCIS, NTNU Gjøvik. WP1 examines vishing and safe-account fraud from both the attacker and the victim perspective and a proposed extension to investment fraud. It distinguishes technical authentication and payment confirmation from legally valid consent.

The research reconstructs how fraud unfolds across channels, while focusing detection and intervention on evidence actually visible to the bank between customer authentication and payment authorisation. Off-bank calls, screen sharing and remote-access activities are described where case sources support them, but are not assumed to be observable by the bank.

The work draws on public decisions of Finansklagenemnda, court judgments, and anonymised or otherwise lawfully accessible cases from SAFE’s banking partners. Results feed into cognitive experiments (WP2), detection research (WP3), scientific publications and a policy white paper.Center for Cyber and Information Security (CCIS) at NTNU will host the SAFE Project.Your immediate leader is head of department.
Duties of the position
• Build a systematically coded corpus of fraud cases from public decisions and lawfully accessible bank material, using a shared template and a cross-channel timeline.
• Develop evidence-based fraud scripts for vishing and safe-account fraud and, subject to scope confirmation, investment fraud, including interim inputs for WP2.
• Map each fraud stage, the channels involved, signs of real-time guidance, and what is actually observable by the bank between authentication and payment authorisation.
• Identify legitimate customer activities with similar bank-visible patterns, to support realistic false-alarm testing without using victim characteristics as automatic detection features.
• Study intervention points and fraudster adaptation, including cases where the bank suspects fraud but the customer rejects warnings; help plan a tabletop session with a banking partner.
• Analyse legal, ethical and governance conditions for collecting, using and sharing fraud-related signals, including privacy, bank confidentiality and interbank cooperation.
• Examine the conditions for transaction warnings, delays, refusals and escalation, with attention to customer consent, liability and loss allocation.
• Assess payee verification and, in investment-fraud cases, checks of providers against Finanstilsynet’s register and market warnings; distinguish these from bank-account verification.
• Provide fraud scripts and realistic look-alike scenarios to WP2 and observability findings, intervention points and lawful-signal constraints to WP3.
• Prepare WP1 deliverables, scientific publications and a policy white paper, and present findings to the SAFE Advisory Board and project partners.
• Contribute, where relevant, to SAFE continuing education (EVU), project reporting and research proposal development.Required selection criteria
• A master’s degree (120 ECTS or equivalent) or a PhD in information security, socio-technical systems, criminology, information systems, law and technology, or a closely related field.
• Documented experience with systematic analysis of qualitative material, such as case files, legal decisions, interviews or incident reports, using a coding scheme or structured method.
• Knowledge of social engineering and fraud in digital channels, such as vishing, authorised push payment fraud or investment fraud.
• Understanding of digital banking and payment processes, including authentication, payment initiation and customer interaction channels.
• Ability to recognise legal, ethical and data-protection questions and work with relevant specialists on their implications for fraud prevention research.
• Reading comprehension of Norwegian or another Scandinavian language sufficient to analyse Norwegian case material and legal decisions.
• Good written and spoken English and the ability to prepare clear, well-structured research reports.Preferred selection criteria
• A PhD in a relevant field, or research experience after completion of the master’s degree.
• Experience in applied research projects involving banks, financial crime specialists or regulatory and legal experts.
• Experience in crime script analysis, situational crime prevention, socio-technical analysis, or process and threat modelling.
• Knowledge of Norwegian or EU rules on payment services, data protection, bank confidentiality or financial crime prevention.
• Experience in fraud prevention, anti-money laundering, compliance or incident handling in the financial sector.
• Experience in planning and facilitating interviews, workshops or tabletop exercises with practitioners.
• Relevant scientific publications or reports on fraud, cybercrime or socio-technical security.
• Skills in structuring and analysing data, for example using Python, R or NVivo.
• Spoken Norwegian or another Scandinavian language for cooperation with partner banks.Personal characteristics
• Highly motivated for applied and collaborative research with financial-sector partners.
• Analytical, structured and precise in the handling of research evidence and sources.
• Discreet and reliable in handling confidential case material and working across disciplines.
• Self-driven, communicative and able to deliver to agreed deadlines.
• Personal suitability will be emphasized.We offer
• Exciting and stimulating research tasks in a strong international academic environment
• Active collaboration with leading industrial and research partners in Norway and abroad.
• A professional and inclusive work environment.
• Favorable terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
• Employee benefits at NTNUSalary and conditions
As a researcher (code 1108/1109) you are normally paid from gross NOK 580 000– NOK 750 000 per annum before tax, depending on qualifications and seniority. As required by law, 2% of this salary will be deducted and paid into the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund.

The engagement is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning State Employees and Civil Servants, and the acts relating to Control of the Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology. Candidates who by assessment of the application and attachment are seen to conflict with the criteria in the latter law will be prohibited from recruitment to NTNU. 

The intended appointment period is 24 months. Starting date at the latest: 1st April 2027.  Please note that loss of external funding is considered equivalent to loss of work assignments, see §19 (1) of the public Employees act. In the event of dismissal by the employer, the notice period is according to §22 (1) of the Public Employers Act. 

It is a prerequisite that you can be present at and accessible to the institution on a daily basis. After the appointment you must assume that there may be changes in the area of work.
About the application
Your application and supporting documentation must be in English. 

The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in  English. 

Please note: the application will only be assessed on the basis of the information we have received by the application deadline. Therefore, make sure that your application clearly shows how your skills and experience meet the criteria described above. The application and all attachments must be sent electronically via Jobbnorge.no. If you are invited to an interview, you must bring certified copies of certificates and diplomas upon request.

If, for any reason, you have taken a career break or have had an atypical career and wish to disclose this in your application, the selection committee will take this into account, recognizing that the quantity of your research may be reduced as a result.

Your application must include:

In the evaluation of which candidate is best qualified, emphasis will be placed on education, experience and personal and interpersonal qualities. Motivation, ambitions, and potential will also count in the assessment of the candidates. Open scientific practice will be recognized.

For the sake of transparency, candidates will be given expert evaluations of their own and other candidates. As an applicant you are considered part of the process and are stipulated by rules of confidentiality. 

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Prof. Stewart James Kowalski, email: stewart.kowalskntnu.no . If you have questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact HR Katrine Rennan, e-mail: katrine.rennan@ntnu.no .
